short: Vietnam's Law on Artificial Intelligence No. 134/2025/QH15, passed on 10 December 2025, has been in force since 1 March 2026; it classes AI systems as high, medium or low risk and leaves fine amounts to Government decree.
title: Vietnam AI Laws
subtitle: The Law on Artificial Intelligence No. 134/2025/QH15, in force from 1 March 2026
body_html:
Status at a glance

Binding AI law in force. The Law on Artificial Intelligence No. 134/2025/QH15 was passed by the 15th National Assembly at its 10th session on 10 December 2025 and has been in force since 1 March 2026 (Art. 34). AI systems already operating when it took effect have a transition period under Art. 35. The law states no fine amounts: the Government sets administrative fines by decree (Art. 29(5)). Verified on 13 November 2026 against the full text published by the Can Tho City Department of Justice.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberDateStatus
Law on Artificial IntelligenceNo. 134/2025/QH15Passed 10 December 2025; in force 1 March 2026In force, with transition periods (Art. 35)
Digital Technology Industry LawNo. 71/2025/QH15Chapter IV and related provisions repealed by Law No. 134/2025/QH15

Who regulates and enforces

  • The state AI authority: may order a system halted or stopped during the transition period if it risks serious harm (Art. 35).
  • The Government: sets the administrative fines by decree (Art. 29(5)).

Scope and reach

The law classes AI systems as high, medium or low risk (Art. 9). Systems already operating when it took effect must comply within 18 months in health, education and finance, and within 12 months in every other field (Art. 35).

Core obligations

  • Compliance with the obligations of a system's risk class (Art. 9), within the transition period for systems already operating (Art. 35).
  • For a high-risk system used correctly that still causes harm, the deployer compensates first and may recover from the provider or developer by agreement (Art. 29).

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
Violations of the lawAdministrative penalties or criminal liability, and civil damages; no fine amount is stated in the law, the Government sets administrative fines by decreeArt. 29, Art. 29(5)The Government; the courts

What is coming next

  • The Government decree setting the administrative fines (Art. 29(5)).
  • The end of the transition periods: 12 months after 1 March 2026 for most systems already operating, and 18 months in health, education and finance (Art. 35).

Related

  • Global AI Laws: every jurisdiction compared, with the world map
  • AI Policy Ledger, the law tracker

Sources

  • Law on Artificial Intelligence No. 134/2025/QH15, full text, Can Tho City Department of Justice (document file)

Last verified

13 November 2026, against the full text above. Not stated in the law and therefore left out: any fine amount, which awaits the Government decree.
